text.howto_turn: Use a free hand at the fixed left indexing selector. Blue A is the original horizontal slider and pin; green B is the original vertical slider and pin. Each stays inside its perpendicular retained channel. The forward vertical guide has a central crossing window, while its long original block remains engaged with the mounted guide segments. One orange original rigid beam joins both continuous pins through two genuinely hollow pivot bores; retaining heads remain attached to their sliders. The beam bars, annular pads and pale off-segment marker P stay rigid together. Sixteen untimed indexed configurations use equal22.5 degree angles. Ideal slider coordinates are A=(240cosangle,0), B=(0,240sinangle) millimetres about the guide crossing; the rigid beam midpoint is(120cosangle,120sinangle), rotating by the negative angle. Its original marker at local+240 follows sampled(360cosangle,-120sinangle), an ellipse with semiaxes360 and120 millimetres. Integer translation tables introduce small measured rounding tolerances; real pivot clearances remain positive. Both original sliders and the original asymmetric beam restore after a full cycle, without a half-turn replacement or reset. Small fixed red backing dots mark the same mathematical XY locus at a different depth, so perspective need not superpose the front marker and a dot in one pixel. This is an indexed geometric exhibit, not pen contact, physical drawing or line creation, a continuously swept constraint/collision solver, force, friction, power transmission, material output, loose-item custody or autonomous timing. Inspect the assembled guide window, depth layers and pin heads from an oblique view; natural overlap can hide individual surfaces.
